title: Short Stuff: The S7VEN Deadly Sins
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Seven Deadly Sins. The hosts open with a playful detour about a "Seven Deadly Zins" wine label and the Seven Deadly Sins in pop culture, including a Gilligan's Island fan theory that maps the characters onto the sins. They note the sins are not in the Bible and trace their origin to the monk Evagrius Ponticus (c. 345 CE), whose list of eight evil thoughts appeared in his Antirrhetikos, written for monks. Pope Gregory the Great later reworked the list into seven principal vices in Moralia in Job, and medieval writers such as Thomas Aquinas popularized it, including the Tree of Vices painted on church walls to aid confession (linked to the 1215 Fourth Lateran Council's annual confession requirement, which the hosts say was twice a year). They mention the Black Death, Chaucer's Parson's Tale, and a 2008 Vatican update listing modern sins such as genetic modification, pollution, social injustice, poverty, obscene wealth, and drug use. Hosts also promote their live tour.
topics: seven deadly sins in pop culture

segments.title: Seven Deadly Zins wine label and opening banter
segments.summary: The hosts joke about a wine brand called Seven Deadly Zins and whether a 'deadly' label is bold. Chuck mentions the Seven Deadly Sins in pop culture.

segments.title: Gilligan's Island sin fan theory
segments.summary: Chuck describes a fan theory mapping Gilligan's Island characters onto the seven sins, with the Professor as Pride, the Skipper as Anger or Wrath, and Gilligan as Sloth.
topics: seven deadly sins in pop culture

segments.title: Live tour promotion
segments.summary: The hosts promote their live tour dates, with tickets on stuffyoushouldknow.com. Cities include Denver, Seattle, San Francisco, Chicago, Madison, Akron, and several Canadian cities.

segments.title: Origins with Evagrius Ponticus
segments.summary: The hosts explain the sins are not in the Bible and that the list traces to the monk Evagrius Ponticus in 345 CE, whose Antirrhetikos first set out eight evil thoughts, originally as a guide for monks.

segments.title: Break and transition to Pope Gregory
segments.summary: After a break, the hosts recap that Evagrius created the list as a monk's roadmap and note that later figures expanded its use.

segments.title: Pope Gregory the Great and Moralia in Job
segments.summary: Pope Gregory the Great, before becoming pope, wrote Moralia in Job, which laid out seven principal vices, including vainglory, envy, anger, melancholy, avarice, gluttony, and lust.

segments.title: Medieval spread and the Tree of Vices
segments.summary: Medieval writers including Thomas Aquinas popularized the list. The Tree of Vices, with pride as the root, was painted on church walls to help people prepare for confession, which the hosts link to the Fourth Lateran Council in 1215.

segments.title: Sin, death, and the Black Death
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how the Black Death heightened preoccupation with sin and the afterlife, and how sermons and Chaucer's Parson's Tale in the Canterbury Tales featured the sins.

segments.title: 2008 Vatican list of modern sins
segments.summary: The hosts note the Catholic Church updated the list in 2008 with modern sins such as genetic modification, human experimentation, pollution, social injustice, poverty, obscene wealth, and drug use.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts wrap up the episode and give the iHeartRadio credit line.
